newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan hints it may stop islands protest boats.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan hints it may stop islands protest boats.

text.p: Taiwan said on Friday that a planned protest voyage to a group of East China Sea islands to challenge Japan's claim of sovereignty might be illegal, hinting that it may act to halt the flotilla.

"According to regulations, if port authorities find illegal activities, they will definitely mete out punishment," Council of Agriculture official Lee Chien-chuan said via the official Central News agency.

Lee, whose agency regulates fishing, said fishing boats were not allowed to ferry non-fishermen and that pleasure boats were not allowed beyond 24 nautical miles off Taiwan's shores -- putting the disputed islands beyond their reach.

Lee said the protest flotilla, planning to try to land on the islands on Monday, would not be eligible for protection by Taiwan marine forces because such service did not extend to pleasure boats straying beyond the 24-mile zone.

Protest leaders have vowed to go ashore on the islands 200 km (140 miles) northeast of Taiwan to remove symbols of Japanese sovereignty from the islands claimed by Tokyo as the Senkakus and by Taiwan and China as the Diaoyus.
